findings.text: The refusal can still be evaded, because it is handed only the TERMINAL identity of a source's successor chain while the cut publishes whatever identity is accepted -- so a waived source whose published identity is an intermediate of that chain classifies 'waived' exactly as before the fix. VERDICT: CONFIRMED, demonstrated. fetch_manifest_source_release_rows (graph_ops.py:12996) sets standard_name_id to terminal.get('target_id'), where the terminal is selected by 'OPTIONAL MATCH path=(start)-[:HAS_SUCCESSOR*0..]->(target) WHERE NOT (target)-[:HAS_SUCCESSOR]->(:StandardName)' ordered depth DESC (graph_ops.py:12959-12969), and _fetch_export_population (export.py:632-635) admits any name whose name_stage is accepted/approved or whose id is in the review batch -- nothing there excludes a name that has a successor. TRIGGERING INPUT 1: waived source 'equilibrium/time_slice/time' with PRODUCED_NAME->x_exported_name (accepted, in the cut) and x_exported_name-[:HAS_SUCCESSOR]->y_pending_successor (name_stage pending, not in the cut). TRIGGERING INPUT 2: the same source with two direct PRODUCED_NAME targets {a_unexported, b_exported_name} and produced_sn_id='a_unexported' -- the ambiguity guard at graph_ops.py:12931 only raises when produced_id is NOT among direct_ids, so this passes and only a_unexported is followed. I ran both through the real resolver with a stubbed client and then through the real _source_disposition: 'intermediate-exported chain: row identity=y_pending_successor published=[b_exported_name, x_exported_name] -> disposition=(waived, )' and 'second direct target: row identity=a_unexported ... -> disposition=(waived, )'. The probe carries a positive control on the same run -- feeding the terminal x_exported_name raises WaivedSourceDeclarationError -- so the two 'waived' results are the guard staying silent, not a blind probe. Log: /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260921T215700385896-opus-review-of-the-stale-waiver-refusal/terminal_only_probe.log; script alongside it.

The second call site -- the pre-staging preflight the commit message advertises as the half that stops a contradicted cut before any domain file is written -- is executed by the gate but its refusal branch is never taken by any test, so deleting the whole block leaves every test green. VERDICT: CONFIRMED by inspection; not mutation-tested (mutating export.py is outside this node's write fence). All four new tests call _source_disposition directly (test_waived_sources.py:184-246); none constructs a manifest row and drives run_export. I enumerated the declaration's 11 waived paths and grepped every tests/standard_names file for them: the only file that both drives run_export with manifest_sources and mentions a declared waived path is test_manifest_generability.py (it uses 'equilibrium/time_slice/constraints/flux_loop/weight'), and that file is green at head -- absent from the node's own 24-id failure set -- so it necessarily takes the non-refusing branch. TRIGGERING INPUT: a later edit that drops lines 3351-3359 (say, while refactoring section 5b) restores publish-then-refuse ordering -- the refusal moves back to line 3437, after _write_domain_yaml at 3404 -- and the focused file still reports 11 passed. What the node's own negative control proved is the decision function's refusal, not this site's.

The refusal does not reach the operator's preflight as a refusal: a dry-run release rehearsal swallows it into a field nothing renders, and the rehearsal reports success. VERDICT: CONFIRMED by inspection of the call path. _rehearse_export_accounting wraps the export leg in 'except Exception as exc: report.accounting_error = ...; logger.warning(...); return' (catalog_release.py:1748-1762), and accounting_error is written only into to_dict() (line 1535) -- grepping imas_codex/ and tests/ finds no CLI or renderer that reads it. TRIGGERING INPUT: 'sn release --dry-run' over a batch whose manifest contains a declared-waived source whose terminal identity is in the cut. The production leg refuses correctly -- the non-dry leg's 'except Exception' appends 'export failed: <message>' to report.errors and returns (catalog_release.py:2039-2041) -- but the rehearsal, which is exactly where an operator looks before spending a real cut, returns a report with empty errors, no exported counts and no source_reconciliation, i.e. the contradiction reads as 'accounting could not be measured'. Before this change a contradicted cut rehearsed with a wrong-but-complete answer; after it, it rehearses with no answer. Neither states the refusal, so the node's invariant stops at the production leg. NOT a scope complaint: catalog_release.py was outside the node's declared write paths, so this belongs in follow_ons.

The commit message's placement claim -- 'before any domain file is written, so a contradicted cut produces no staging artifact' -- is true of what the cut WRITES and false of what it LEAVES: the previous catalog tree is already deleted by the time the refusal fires, and no export report is written to say why. VERDICT: CONFIRMED by ordering. Section 4 runs 'shutil.rmtree(sn_dir)' at export.py:3162 over staging_dir/standard_names; the new preflight is at 3351; the first _write_domain_yaml is at 3404. Every other refusal in run_export that can fire after the staging dir exists calls staging_path.mkdir + _write_export_report before returning (3132-3135, 3149-3151, 3377-3379); this one raises instead, so the report is not written. TRIGGERING INPUT: a second release attempt into the standing staging dir from get_sn_staging_dir() whose manifest carries a contradicted waiver -- the prior cut's standard_names/*.yaml is gone and staging holds no export_report explaining the refusal. Severity is low because staging is regenerable and the release leg preserves the message in report.errors; the finding is that the stated invariant is narrower than written, which matters because the loader-level refusal at 2902 genuinely does hold it ('before any staging output exists') and the new one is documented as if it did too.

The refusal message offers the human exactly two explanations, and a third is at least as likely in this graph, so the message can misdirect the reconciliation it demands. VERDICT: NIT on the wording, not the control flow. The text asserts 'The declaration entry is stale ... or the composition that produced the identity is wrong.' TRIGGERING INPUT: a waived source whose chain was folded onto an identity a DIFFERENT source also produces -- the many-to-many PRODUCED_NAME shape that dedup folds routinely create -- and that peer's identity is what the cut carries. Then the declaration is NOT stale (this source still yields nothing nameable on its own) and the composition that produced the identity is NOT wrong (it belongs to the peer); what is wrong is the binding of this source to that terminal. The refusal is still correct -- two sources of truth do disagree and a human must look -- but a reader following the message's two branches will find both false and have no third to check. Naming the terminal chain and its other producers in the message would close it.

justifications.durability: This is where the change is thinner than it reads, and all three findings are about what the guard cannot see rather than what it does wrong. (1) Its input is the successor-chain TERMINAL, while the cut publishes accepted identities that may sit mid-chain, and the multi-target ambiguity check only fires when produced_sn_id is absent from direct_ids -- so two concrete graph shapes reproduce the original silent 'waived' verdict, which I demonstrated against the real resolver and the real decision function with a positive control on the same run. (2) The preflight call site's refusal branch has no test, so the half of the fix that orders the refusal before the write can be deleted without turning the gate red. (3) The refusal never reaches the dry-run rehearsal as a refusal, because catalog_release swallows it into an unrendered accounting_error. What IS durable: the refusal is one function called from both sites, so the two cannot drift apart; it reuses WaivedSourceDeclarationError, so every caller that already handles a bad declaration handles this; and the three non-refusing cases are pinned by tests a future edit cannot quietly widen past. A new declaration entry added tomorrow inherits the guard automatically, since membership is read from the YAML rather than enumerated in code.
justifications.evidence: Among the strongest evidence records I have audited on this plan, and it survives independent re-measurement. The node declared its negative control with a named mutation (restore the pre-fix waived-first order), reported exactly one failure at exit 1 naming test_a_waiver_that_reached_an_exported_name_refuses, and recorded a byte-identical sha256 for export.py before and after -- that is a control that could have failed and a restoration that can be checked. Base and head suites were both run on all_debug under a pinned SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1758412800, both completed with their totals lines, and the failure-id sets are identical at 24 ids with passes rising 7618 -> 7622, exactly the four tests added. I re-ran the focused gate myself at the merged head 750ce1b9d: 'uv run --no-sync pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/standard_names/test_waived_sources.py' -> 11 passed, 1 warning in 9.97s (log in the run dir), against the 7 the node reports at base. I also confirmed the 24-id base set is genuinely pre-existing rather than a red base the node created -- it contains test_export_exclusion_ledger and test_export_exit_accounting ids that have nothing to do with waivers. Marked down two points for one absence the record does not acknowledge: no evidence exercises the run_export preflight's refusal branch (finding 2), so the 'before any domain file is written' half of the claim rests on reading the line numbers, which is what I had to do to check it.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for this file and for the surface it defends. The refusal raises the same WaivedSourceDeclarationError the loader raises for a self-contradictory declaration (both lists naming one path), so 'the declaration disagrees with itself' keeps one error type and one handler at every caller; a new exception class here would have split that. Putting the decision in _source_disposition and driving that same function from the preflight is the right shape -- the alternative, an inline comparison at the preflight, is exactly how two sites drift. The docstrings argue in mechanism terms ('two sources of truth about one source', 'neither fact may win quietly') rather than citing a plan or a reviewer, and the test comments do the same. The message names both the source path and the identity, which is the minimum a human needs to start. Docked lightly for the message's two-cause framing (finding 5) and for documenting a placement guarantee the code holds only for newly written files (finding 4).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node was to stop a stale waiver hiding a name that the cut carries, and to refuse the contradiction rather than reorder which wrong answer a reader gets. It did precisely that. At 750ce1b9d the waived branch of _source_disposition (export.py:2801-2803) tests 'standard_name_id is not None and standard_name_id in exported_ids' before returning ('waived',''), raising through the single helper _refuse_waiver_that_reached_a_name (2757-2780), and the same decision function is driven a second time over a supplied manifest at 3351-3359 so the refusal precedes the first _write_domain_yaml at 3404. The reported defect still reproduces at the base revision: I re-derived it from the shipped source rather than trusting the record -- at 485836e4d the waived branch is an unconditional 'return "waived", ""' (git show 485836e4d:imas_codex/standard_names/export.py), so the reproduction the node quoted (source_path and standard_name_id both present, identity in exported_ids, result ('waived','')) is what that code returns. Three non-refusing cases the fix must not disturb are each pinned by a test and each passes. Marked down from full only because the invariant as WRITTEN in the docstring ('a source that is both declared waived and carried by the cut') is broader than the invariant IMPLEMENTED, which is 'declared waived and whose successor-chain terminal is carried' -- see finding 1, where two graph shapes satisfy the written rule and pass the implemented one.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exact. The declared write paths were export.py, test_waived_sources.py and the two plan/evidence documents, and 'git show --stat' over both commits shows those four files and nothing else: export.py +48, test_waived_sources.py +66, the archive anchor +57, the plan +9. No line is deleted anywhere -- both commits are pure additions -- so nothing peer-owned could have been displaced. waived_sources.yaml is untouched, which matters: the cheapest way to make a contradicted cut go away would have been to edit the declaration, and the node did not reach for it. Both commits carry a conventional subject and a body, neither carries AI attribution or a plan identifier, and the new symbol _refuse_waiver_that_reached_a_name is named for what it does. The one genuinely adjacent defect I found (finding 3, the dry-run rehearsal) sits in catalog_release.py, outside the fence, and the node correctly did not reach into it -- I report it as a follow-on rather than as a miss.
